The 2026.9 changelog (8 September) lists no bookkeeping export change at all, so the rework cannot be the cause. First action is Administration -> Jobs to read the job state, not the rework diff; and the re-run has to cover 5 August onward, because the doc is explicit that failed or missed windows are not picked up automatically. Ulrika needs September in the ledger before the end of the month.
items.action: Check Administration -> Jobs for the tenant's bookkeeping export job state, re-enable it, and re-run from 5 August onward rather than September only; then reply on the existing email thread correcting the staging-table theory.

proposal.subject: Re: September disbursements missing from our ledger
proposal.body:
Hej,

We have found the cause and it is not the staging-table rework, so I want to correct what we told you last week.

The nightly bookkeeping export job was switched off on the evening of 5 August, while we were debugging the duplicate rows in the July file. It was never switched back on. That is why your last file is dated 4 August and why nothing has failed and nobody has had an error: a disabled job writes no file and raises no alert, because from the platform's point of view nothing went wrong. Your own observation — no transfers rather than failed transfers — was the right clue.

What we are doing:

1. Re-enabling the job and confirming in the job log that it shows as enabled.
2. Re-running the export for the whole missing window, 5 August to date, not just September. Missed nights are not picked up automatically, so this has to be an explicit re-run. Re-runs arrive with an _r2 suffix in the file name so your accountant can tell them apart from the originals.
3. Confirming to you, with the run log, that there is a file for every night in the window before we consider this closed.

We will have the back-run in place in time for the quarter close. The duplicate-row defect and the blank cost centres on split-year rows are separate items and I am following those up separately, with ticket references, so you have something written down.

We also owe you the safeguard we discussed on 11 August: you are told if the job is off for more than two nights. That did not exist, which is the reason a switched-off job could go unnoticed for five weeks. I will confirm when it does.

Apologies for the detour via the rework.

proposal.subject: Re: The portal loses documents on submit — where we actually are
proposal.body:
Hej,

A straight update on the lost documents, because our answers to you have not been consistent and you should know that.

Where we are: this is not confirmed as your PDF template. The upload path does a size check, a MIME type check and a virus scan, and it does not convert or re-render, so a file that opens differently in different readers would still pass. Our documentation also states that an upload is never discarded without the applicant being told — there is supposed to be no path where a file is accepted by the browser and then silently disappears. Your applicants describe exactly that path, four times this year, which means either something is happening we cannot yet account for, or the error is being shown and not understood. Either way it is ours to explain, not yours to fix by buying a new PDF tool.

What we are doing now: we are pulling the server-side upload records for the case forwarded to support on 15 September — the applicant name is enough for us to find the record, and we will take it from there. We will come back with what the server actually saw for that submission: whether an upload ticket was issued, whether chunks arrived, and whether an error was returned.

What would help, if it happens again during the closing days: the application reference and roughly what time it was submitted. Either the applicant name or the reference is fine — you should not have to chase applicants for a number.

Two practical things before the 30th:

- The reload workaround still holds. If an applicant has had the form open for a long time, reloading the page before attaching and submitting has worked in every case we have seen.
- Please keep the current arrangement of accepting files by email as a fallback, but let us know each time it is used, so the count is ours to carry rather than yours.

We know half the applications arrive in the last 48 hours. We will watch the queue across the 29th and 30th and respond to anything from you on those two days as priority.

Apologies that this has been open since July with the assumption pointed at your side of it.

proposal.subject: Batch invite before the 22nd — written steps and the greyed-out button
proposal.body:
Hej,

The expression-of-interest deadline is on Tuesday, so I want the batch invite settled before then rather than on a call afterwards.

The steps, in writing:

1. Open the list view for the round and filter to the expressions of interest you want to invite.
2. Tick the rows, or use the header checkbox to select all filtered rows.
3. Open the actions menu at the top right of the list — this is the part that is not obvious — and choose "Bjud in valda".
4. Confirm the invitation template and send. Invitations go out as one batch and each invited applicant gets their own stage-two link.

On the case from 24 August, where the button is greyed out for one user: that is almost certainly a permission on the role rather than a fault in the function, and it is exactly the user who needs it. We are reproducing it today and will correct the role. If for any reason it is not fixed before the deadline, we will run the batch from our side on your instruction so that nobody has to click through sixty invitations.

Apologies that this was left to a demonstration that never happened, and that the August case sat without an answer.

If you would like, we can also do a five-minute dry run on a couple of test rows before Tuesday so you have seen it work with your own login.

proposal.subject: Re: Material before the October board meeting
proposal.body:
Hej,

Apologies for the delay in answering this. Here is what you will have and when.

You will have the complete pack by Friday 25 September, a week before your 2 October deadline, as three pages:

1. The integration one-pager. What the nightly bookkeeping export does, which transaction types it writes, what it replaces in manual work, and an honest estimate of hours saved per payment run, with the assumptions shown so your board can argue with them. It will also state plainly that the integration is bespoke code maintained by us and therefore does not carry the same automated test coverage as the standard product — that was the question asked in July and the answer has not changed.

2. Where the platform is going. The roadmap note already sent, with the two points that matter written down rather than relayed verbally: the two-way accounting sync is on next year's plan and is not a commitment, and if it is built it will likely carry an additional cost that we cannot quantify yet. We would rather your board hear that from us than have it softened in the retelling.

3. Support response times, with numbers and not an apology. First-response times on each case opened since June, the agreed target of one business day, which cases missed it and by how much, the specific reason the nine-day case sat as long as it did, and the two changes now in place: a named contact for your account and an automatic flag to the support lead for any unassigned case older than two days.

We will also include, unprompted, a short note on the bookkeeping export gap since 4 August: what caused it, what we have done, and what we have put in place so a disabled job cannot go unnoticed again. It belongs in the pack. Leaving it out would make the rest less credible.

One request: could we move our October check-in to the week of 28 September rather than early October? That way we can walk through the pack together while there is still time to change it, instead of after the papers have gone out. Any slot that week works for us.

proposal.subject: Re: Response times on our tickets — what happened, and where each case stands
proposal.body:
Hej,

This is the written answer promised on 2 September, and it is late. It was given verbally at a catch-up on 15 September, which meant the person who asked the question was not in the room. That was our mistake and this puts it right.

The nine-day case, the report footer showing the wrong organisation name: it arrived on a Friday afternoon. It was picked up the same day by a colleague who then went on leave without reassigning it, and the case sat in a personal queue where nobody else saw it. It was not triaged as low priority and it was not a difficult question. Nothing was decided about it — it was simply invisible. The fix has since shipped and has been confirmed at your end.

What has changed, concretely:

- Any case that is unassigned or untouched for more than two days is now flagged automatically to the support lead. This is live.
- Your account has a named contact who picks up anything unanswered by lunchtime the following day.

The agreed target is one business day for a first response. We did not meet it in August and we will include the actual figures in the board material rather than a general statement.

A status on each open case, which was promised for 17 August and not delivered:

- Documents lost on submit (open since 24 July): being worked on now against a specific case, with a written update to follow separately. This one has been open too long.
- Board report with grantee organisation number: an estimate was promised within two weeks on 19 August and has not arrived. We are giving you a date this week.
- Applicant mail templates with last year's hard-coded dates: one template corrected, three still to do, and we will book the short call needed to finish them.
- September invoice missing the VAT line: being corrected, see the separate reply on that case.
- Bookkeeping export gap since 4 August: cause found, correction in progress, written update sent separately.

You said in August that you would see how September went. This is September's account of itself, including the parts that do not favour us.

proposal.subject: Programme budget frame — confirming what is live in production
proposal.body:
Hej,

One loose end we want to close properly before decisions start in this round.

The annual budget frame with warning mode was set up in your test environment in August, and you asked for it to be switched on in production for both programmes. That case was closed on your message, and we cannot see a record of anyone confirming the production change — so rather than assume, we have checked it and are confirming it directly.

What is now set in production, for both programmes:

- Annual frame: the ceiling figure your board has set for each programme. Please confirm the amounts are the ones you want us to hold.
- Behaviour when the frame is passed: warning at decision time, not a block. The caseworker sees the warning and can still proceed deliberately.
- Counter basis: approved decisions in the current year. Drafts are not counted.

If you would rather have a hard block for one of the programmes, that is a single setting and we can change it before the decision meetings.

Going forward we will not close a case on a request to change something in production until the change has been made and confirmed back to you. That is on us.
